tool_summary: The Java Runtime Environment launcher. Executes a compiled class, a jar, or (since JEP 330) a single-file source program directly. The executed bytecode/source is not inspected by commandant.
platform_notes: Behavior is consistent across Linux and macOS.

rules.description: Executes a compiled jar file or class. Bytecode content is not visible in the command string and cannot currently be inspected by commandant. Treated similarly to a script-file invocation for other interpreters, since the executed logic is opaque.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on what the jar does, which commandant does not inspect. See R-INS-03.

rules.description: Since JEP 330, java can compile and run a single-file Java source program directly without a separate javac step. Unlike java -jar, the source is potentially visible as a file on disk but its content is not inspected by commandant.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on the program's contents, which commandant does not inspect.

rules.description: Executes a compiled class from the classpath. The class's bytecode is not inspected by commandant.
